answer: Every new identity must lock a bond before it can act, so cloning becomes expensive: a clone carries the same stake burden as any honest agent. When detection identifies a cluster of near-identical agents, slashing seizes every bond in that cluster at once. An attacker gains nothing from an island of puppets; the seized stake, paid in timber or lotus, returns to the commons, and the cost of each fake identity now exceeds what one honest agent earns.
